title: Log a skipped import once, with everything needed to fix it

blocks.text: An energy company imports electricity meter readings every night, one file per region. A file with a line that isn't a reading is skipped and tried again the next night, after someone has fixed it. The operations team counts the job's log records at `WARNING` and above to decide how many files need a person in the morning, and the person then needs to find the broken line from the log alone.
Finish `importFile` and `runNightly` in `src/main/java/practice/MeterImport.java`. The logger is `MeterImport.LOG` (`java.util.logging`). About ten lines in total.

cases.says: a file of readings is added up and nothing is logged as a problem
a file with an unreadable line is skipped and the problem is logged
one skipped file produces exactly one log record at WARNING or above
the log record carries the ImportException itself, naming the file and the line
the logged exception's cause chain reaches the NumberFormatException for the bad line

origin.section: Log an Exception Where It Is Handled, Never Where It Is Rethrown

concepts: An exception is logged once, with its stack trace, by the layer that handles it; lower layers add context to the exception they throw instead of logging.
